title: Route is not covered through Django URL resolution
reasoning: The feature being reviewed is the public route /api/fasts/by-feast-date/, but the included tests instantiate FastByFeastDateView directly and call get_queryset() rather than issuing a request through the Django URL dispatcher. That means a regression in the URL pattern, route name, trailing slash behavior, or APIView dispatch/serialization layer could pass these tests while breaking the advertised endpoint.
recommendation: Add at least one API client test that calls /api/fasts/by-feast-date/?date=<iso-date> and asserts the expected HTTP status and response payload, preferably also covering the missing/invalid date validation over the real route.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current FastByFeastDateView tests build an APIRequestFactory request and assign it directly to a manually constructed view instance, so they bypass hub/urls.py and DRF dispatch.
suggestedRegressionTest: Use self.client.get('/api/fasts/by-feast-date/', {'date': self.feast_date_1.isoformat()}) in hub/tests/test_fast_views.py and assert HTTP 200 with the expected fast in response.data.
minimumFixScope: Add URL-level coverage for FastByFeastDateView in hub/tests/test_fast_views.py.
